subject: Clinical data lifecycle: retention limits, redaction & deletion options

Subject: Clinical data - retention & redaction requirements

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme's security team asked me to follow up with concrete questions about retention and redaction for clinical PII/PHI when using Redwood's hosted and private offerings. High-level asks:

- Maximum retention we can configure for identifiable clinical records (by env: hosted vs private).
- Options for field-level redaction vs pseudonymization for downstream model training and caching.
- How deletion requests are handled end-to-end (including backups and logs) and SLAs for erasure.
- Any limits or caveats around legal hold / investigatory retention.

Can you share a short playbook or bullets we can share with InfoSec and Legal? We're under a tight timeline for procurement (contract signature targeted by Aug 20).

Appreciate it —
Elena

Subject: Re: Clinical data - retention & redaction requirements

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik (infra/serving) and Naomi (legal) for details. Below is a compact response; we'll attach a one-page playbook and a proposed retention matrix.

Short answers (high level):
- Retention limits: Hosted API (default) supports tenant-configurable retention windows down to 0 days; for regulated accounts we recommend Private or Dedicated where retention is customer-controlled and can be set to strict minima (e.g., 30/90/365 days) based on your policy.
- Redaction options: field-level tokenization/pseudonymization, deterministic hashing for linkage, one-way hashing for irreversible de-identification, and structured field suppression. We also support client-side tokenization before sending to the service.
- Deletion workflow: immediate logical deletion request -> purge from hot stores within SLA window (24-72 hours depending on plan) -> scheduled background purge from caches and async queues -> backup retention window purge (can be configured, default 30 days) -> audit log entry with deletion-id.
- Legal hold: hold overrides deletion; we provide tools to flag customer datasets as "under legal hold" which prevents automated purge until release. This is surfaced in our Console and in audit logs.

See attached for a drafted retention matrix and redaction patterns we recommend for clinical fields. Karthik and Naomi — can you add technical and legal constraints?

Thanks,
Priyom
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clinical data - retention & redaction requirements

Elena — technical details below, called out by capability and recommended default for regulated clinical workloads: 

1) Namespace & storage separation
- For Private/Dedicated customers we provision isolated namespaces (separate S3 buckets, KV stores) so retention/deletion policies are enforceable at storage-level. Hosted customers get logical separation; physical co-tenancy is possible but we apply strict tenant ACLs. Recommendation: Acme pick Private for PHI to get hardware/network isolation.

2) Redaction options (how they behave and tradeoffs)
- Field suppression: remove fields entirely before persistence. Pros: simplest, irreversible; Cons: loses context for model prompts.
- Deterministic pseudonymization: replace identifiers with stable tokens (e.g., PATIENT_12345). Pros: preserves linkage across records; Cons: reversible if mapping stored insecurely. Mapping is stored in a customer-specific encrypted KV (optional).
- One-way hashing (SHA-256 + salt): irreversible for practical use; good when linkage not required.
- Format-preserving pseudonymization: keeps field shape (dates -> date buckets) to preserve model signals.
- Client-side encryption + tokenization: ideal for maximum control; Redwood never sees plaintext.

3) Caching and KV cache handling
- Inference KV cache and prefix cache can retain transient data. We provide APIs to invalidate cache entries on deletion events. For regulated workloads, we recommend disabling persistent prefix caching or setting TTLs <= 24 hours.

4) Backup + snapshot retention
- Backups are retained for a configurable window (default 30 days for hosted). For Private we can contractually reduce to 7 days with additional attestations; extremes (0 days) require additional operational controls and are available for enterprise agreements.

5) Deletion SLA details
- Hot-layer purge: within 24 hours for Dedicated/Private; 72 hours typical for hosted.
- Backup/snapshots purge: dependent on configured backup window. Physical media destruction (if applicable) follows standard cloud provider timelines; we can include contractual commitments for onsite/on-prem appliances.

6) Auditability
- Every deletion request gets a deletion-id, timestamp, operator id, and retention policy applied. Audit exports can be pushed to your SIEM.

I'll attach a short redaction proposal (examples keyed to common clinical fields) and a script snippet for our delete API.

—Karthik
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Elena — quick legal point-of-view and an ask to finalize procurement language.

- We can commit to contractual retention windows and backup windows in the MSA (e.g., host: 30/90/365; private: configurable to customer minima). For PHI, recommend Private deployment with explicit SLA clauses for deletion timelines (hot purge <= 24h; backup purge within 7-30 days per selected option).
- Legal hold: we will include an explicit exception flow. Customer must provide legal hold ID and scope; Redwood will suspend automated purges and provide audit evidence. Release requires signed confirmation.
- Certifications & evidence: we can provide SOC 2 Type II reports and an attestation of deletion workflows. For highly regulated clients we can provide runbooks and, where needed, onsite audits under NDA.

Next steps:
1) Priyom — please share the one-page playbook with the highlighted rows we recommend for Acme (I suggest 30-day backup window + deterministic pseudonymization for our baseline).
2) Elena — if you can confirm which fields Acme needs linkage for (e.g., patient ID) vs which can be irreversible, Naomi will draft the MSA retention sections.

I'll also propose specific contract language for the deletion SLA and legal-hold flow and attach it to the procurement packet.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
